01 · The community

A network of young people who change their own city

The Global Shapers Community brings together young people aged 18 to 30 in Hubs, one per city. The action is local; the network is global.

10k+Shapers under 30
~500Hubs worldwide
150+countries
2011year founded, in Geneva
since 1971

World Economic Forum

An independent, not-for-profit organisation that brings together governments, business, academia and civil society. Best known for its Annual Meeting in Davos every January.

founded it and supports it with staff, funding and technology
since 2011

Global Shapers Community

An independent, not-for-profit and non-partisan foundation headquartered in Geneva. A network of volunteers organised in Hubs, like Hub Yola.

You are a volunteer of a Hub, not an employee of the Forum.

02 · Mission and values

Three verbs guide everything

These are the community’s three strategic objectives. Every opportunity you will come across fits at least one of them.

Develop Youth Leaders
Develop

young leaders. You grow as a leader by doing, making mistakes and collaborating with people different from you.

Where you live it: Hub meetings, leadership roles, retreats.

Accelerate Youth Action
Accelerate

youth action. Ideas become projects with measurable impact in the city.

Where you live it: Hub Projects and cross-Hub initiatives.

Amplify Youth Voices
Amplify

youth voices. What we learn here reaches global conversations.

Where you live it: Forum events, articles, Flagship Collaborations.

the 5 values you will always hear about:

PassionEnergy to start and to not give up halfway.
IntegrityDoing the right thing, transparently, even with no audience.
ServiceThe impact is for people outside the Hub, not for us.
CooperationWe decide and act together. Leadership is shared.
CommitmentShowing up, delivering and keeping your word.
The impact model

Change happens in a cycle

This is the Impact Model from the official guides: each part feeds the next, and the global network returns learning to every Shaper.

03 · Who’s who

From your Hub to Geneva

The model is decentralised: the Hub decides and acts. Each level above exists to support, not to command.

Foundation Board

Oversees the community’s mission and governance.

HQ in Geneva

The community team inside the Forum. Your Community Manager shows up as “Forum Contact” on your profile.

Community Champion

Experienced volunteer who supports the Hubs in your sub-region.

Hub Curatorship

The trio that leads the Hub for one year, from 1 July to 30 June.

You, Global Shaper

Member of Hub Yola, with a voice and a vote. A Hub has 20 to 50 people.

World Economic Forum

Founded the community and supports HQ with staff, funding and systems. It does not run the Hub.

Alumni

Anyone who has turned 30 or completed 5 years in the community. Helps when the Hub asks, but does not vote or interfere in decisions.

Who do I talk to?

  1. Day-to-day questions, meetings, projects Curatorship
  2. Conflict, elections, retreat Champion
  3. HQ, events, visas, partnerships Community Manager

Curator

the Hub’s “president”

Looks after governance, is the main contact with HQ, manages the Hub page on Forum Spaces and attends GSAS in Geneva.

Vice-Curator

the day-to-day engine

Facilitates meetings and activities, leads recruitment, runs the Twin Cities programme and stands in for the Curator when needed.

Impact Officer

the guardian of impact

Ensures at least 1 project a year, with indicators, and records the projects on Forum Spaces.

04 · Your journey

From selection to Alumni

Six stops. The fourth is the one that counts: your official membership starts the day your Forum Spaces account is created.

  1. 1

    Selection

    Form, video and an interview with a panel of 3+ people.

  2. 2

    Probation

    A trial period, if the Hub uses one. No vote yet.

  3. 3

    Onboarding

    Induction day, a buddy and this guide.

  4. 4

    Forum Spaces

    Account created: you are an official Shaper. You must be aged 18 to 27 on that date.

  5. 5

    Life in the Hub

    Meetings, projects, leadership and events.

  6. 6

    Alumni

    At 30, or after 5 years in the community, whichever comes first.

Moved to another city?

Ask the Community Manager for a transfer, with a short justification and both Hubs’ Curators in copy. With both Curators’ “ok”, the change shows up on Forum Spaces within a week.

Life got busy?

Talk to the Curatorship. The Charter allows a temporary break. Leaving before meeting the Alumni criteria closes your account and gives no access to the Alumni network.

When do I become Alumni?

Ask the Global Shapers Assistant, the chatbot in the corner of Forum Spaces:

“I joined on DD/MM/YYYY and was born on DD/MM/YYYY. When do I become eligible for Alumni?”
05 · The deal

Three numbers to remember

By joining, you agree to the Community Charter, which applies to every Hub in the world. This is the yearly minimum.

60%

attendance at the Hub’s local meetings and activities over the year.

1

Hub project or leadership role per year, at minimum.

2months

to adjust, after a conversation, before any cancellation. With the right to appeal.

Forum Spaces always up to date The Forum’s Code of Conduct, social media included No using the Hub for party-political purposes Read your Hub’s local charter

Why the Hub is the way it is

The Charter’s composition rules. They explain many decisions in the selection process.

06 · The Shaper’s year

The year runs from July to June

The calendar follows the Curatorship’s term, not the calendar year. The big rite is the February election.

  1. Jul–Augplan

    1 July: Curatorship and Champion terms begin. Newly elected Curators go to GSAS in Geneva. Retreats set the year’s goals.

  2. Sep–Octmobilise

    Applications open for Davos. Recruitment and arrival of new members. Alumni Celebration Day in October.

  3. Nov–Deccelebrate

    Those selected for Davos are announced in the Newsletter. Project Showcase regional in December.

  4. Jan–Marelect

    Annual Meeting in Davos (Jan). Elections in February, with results by 1 March. The incoming Curatorship shadows the current one.

  5. Apr–Junpass the baton

    May is the Month of Impact. In June: Annual Review, Youth Pulse Survey and AMNC in China. On the 30th, terms end.

Global Shapers Assistant · how can I help?

Build your profile today

  • Face photo, in colour, front-facing, professional
  • Correct date of birth and personal details
  • Personal email, not your work one
  • Bio of 200 to 300 words, in the third person
  • App installed and notifications set up

The bio formula

1Current job title and organisation
2Areas of expertise, with keywords
3Achievements with numbers
4Leadership, education and languages

Why it matters: when the Forum looks for Shapers for a panel, a consultation or an event, it searches profiles by keyword. An empty profile is a missed opportunity.

Who looks after what

Curator: Hub page and members Impact Officer: Hub projects You: your profile Technical problem: digitalsupport@weforum.org
08 · Impact projects

The heart of the Hub

Every Hub delivers at least 1 project a year, with measurable impact recorded on Forum Spaces. And you take part in at least one.

The test: did the project improve the life of someone outside the Hub?

Counts

  • At least 3 Hub members, with a goal, deadline and team
  • Benefits people outside the Hub
  • Non-partisan and aligned with the values
  • Measurable result
  • Created by the Hub or in partnership, with the Hub leading

Doesn’t count

  • A personal project of one Shaper alone
  • A benefit that stays among Shapers only
  • Action with a party-political slant
  • A one-day event with no measured result
  • Retreats and Meet the Leaders (very valuable, but they don’t replace the project)

a project in 5 steps

ConceiveFind a real problem together with the people who live it
PlanSMART goal, template, team in place
ExecuteLaunch, mobilise allies, adjust
EvaluateMeasure with indicators and hold a debrief
ShowRecord on Forum Spaces, say thank you, spread the word
the problem formula (the same as the official form)

[beneficiary] in [place] needs [to do this] so that [this result is achieved].

Illustrative example: young people aged 16 to 24 in [community] need digital skills training to land a first job. Indicator: [no.] young people trained by [month].

and how the community measures all this: the Theory of Change

Activities 1

What we do. Trainings, resources, events and project support.

Outputs 2

What we deliver. More skills, amplified voices, more local projects.

Outcomes 3

What changes. Stronger leaders and people reached by projects.

Impact 4

The difference we make. Young people with a decisive role in the present and the future.

37 indicators in total. An honest reminder from the official guide: we are volunteers, not a development agency. Plan with the hours the team really has.

How to get to Davos (or China)

Any active Shaper on Forum Spaces can apply, including people who just joined. Curators get no priority. Calls go out in the monthly Newsletter.

  1. Profile up to dateWithout an active profile, or with a bio that doesn’t match the application, it isn’t even assessed.
  2. Video of up to 60 seconds, in EnglishShow your impact with numbers, not awards. Polished production is not needed.
  3. Scores from 1 to 5At least 2 reviewers read each application.
  4. BalanceGender, region and, in general, one Shaper per Hub.
  5. CostsRegistration covered; flights and hotel for those who need it, if funds allow. Visa and meals are on you.
10 · Communication and brand

You speak for your Hub, never for the whole community

You can

  • Use the Hub Yola logo on Hub materials
  • List Global Shapers on LinkedIn as volunteer work
  • Give your personal opinion, making clear it is yours
  • Post with #GlobalShapers and #ShapersImpact and tag the official profiles
  • Use the Global Shapers Community logo with written permission

You can’t

  • Use the World Economic Forum logo
  • Say you work at the Forum or list it as a job
  • Position the Hub in party politics
  • Recreate, recolour or distort any logo
  • Approach Forum partners without consulting HQ first

I am a member of Hub Yola of the Global Shapers Community, a network founded by the World Economic Forum.

Partnerships

Every profit goes back into projects. No partnerships with arms, gambling, human rights violations, pornography or tobacco. Partnering with a member’s organisation only with the Hub’s consensus approval.

Document it

After every call, send a summary email. Formalise with a cooperation agreement. Consult the Hub before closing any deal.

Community colours

Use on official materials, without altering the logos.

#0038A8#7AB1E8#A6A6A9

Data: no open spreadsheets with Shapers’ contacts and no group link anyone can join.
